bull.b: The statistically significant primary endpoint provides a defined clinical value proposition for Deramiocel in DMD. If confirmed through FDA review, it could support approval for an upper-limb skeletal-muscle indication and establish a focused commercial opportunity.

Broad treatment exposure and long-term follow-up strengthen the program’s safety database and reduce clinical execution uncertainty. This experience can support regulatory discussions, physician confidence and future development of related cell- and exosome-based therapies.

Operational internal manufacturing can improve control over supply, quality and launch execution if approval is obtained. The sizable liquidity reserve also gives Capricor flexibility to fund regulatory, manufacturing and commercial preparations over the near term.

bear.b: Capricor has not yet demonstrated commercial scale and remains dependent on a successful product launch to create revenue. Rising operating costs and widening losses increase the amount of capital required before the business can become self-sustaining.

The negative advisory vote weakens the case for the originally targeted cardiomyopathy use and creates approval and label uncertainty. Although non-binding, it may narrow the initial market and require additional data, analysis or regulatory negotiation.

bear.t: Persistent Cash Burn and Rising Leverage
bear.b: Sustained negative cash generation means Capricor may need additional financing before reaching commercialization or profitability. Rising debt adds obligations to a loss-making business and could reduce financial flexibility if regulatory timelines or launch costs extend.
